Convert spherical to Cartesian coordinates (radians)

Source: R/dir-utils.R
SphToCart.Rd

Converts a line or plane orientation given in spherical coordinates (trend/plunge or strike/dip) to direction cosines in a North–East–Down coordinate system.

Usage

SphToCart(trd, plg, k = 0)

Arguments

trd

Numeric. Trend of the line (radians, k = 0) or strike of the plane (radians, right-hand rule, k = 1).

plg

Numeric. Plunge of the line (radians, k = 0) or dip of the plane (radians, k = 1).

k

Integer. 0 for a line (trend/plunge); 1 for a plane (strike/dip, right-hand rule). Default 0.

Value

A named numeric vector c(cn, ce, cd) with the north, east, and down direction cosines.

References

Allmendinger, R. W., Cardozo, N., & Fisher, D. M. (2012). Structural geology algorithms: Vectors and tensors. Cambridge university press.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Triple colon required because it's not exported
GMisc:::SphToCart(trd = pi / 4, plg = pi / 6)
GMisc:::SphToCart(trd = pi / 3, plg = pi / 5, k = 1)
} # }
